family_chandelier.name: Family Chandelier
family_chandelier.description: A chandelier that IS a scene tree: grab the button and one mid node swings - and its whole subtree swings rigidly with it, because children live in their parent's transform. add_child made brass. Graph taxonomy rung 2, 2026-08-27.

postman_of_paths.name: Postman Of Paths
postman_of_paths.description: A letter walking a NodePath along glowing ropes between mailboxes - up through '..', down through names, the address printed as it goes. To reach is to traverse. Graph taxonomy rung 3, 2026-08-27.

ouroboros_signals.name: Ouroboros Signals
ouroboros_signals.description: Three telephones in a ring, a call circling forever - connect() permits the cycle the tree refuses, shown beside a small rigid tree with one dashed refused edge. Graph taxonomy rung 4, 2026-08-27.

wallflower_and_star.name: Wallflower And Star
wallflower_and_star.description: A dance floor: one node holding twelve ribbons, a wallflower holding one. Degree as social gravity, counted at their feet. Graph taxonomy rung 6, 2026-08-27.

archipelago_wedding.name: Archipelago Wedding
archipelago_wedding.description: Two islands of lamps, each glowing its component's colour - press the button and a drawbridge edge marries them into one gold. Union-find as a wedding. Graph taxonomy rung 7, 2026-08-27.

seven_bridges.name: Seven Bridges to Walk
seven_bridges.description: Euler's question at the size of a body: a city 12 x 14 m on the floor, built from the spatial lab's prefabs through the lab's own adapter - shores fenced with the blue DO NOT CROSS barrier, the edge with concrete barriers, nine bridge places over channels two metres wide, each bridge its own construction (a panel between crate stalls, planks between concrete parapets, planks with plank rails, two walkable wedges a metre high, a ten-metre plank footbridge) - where the walk is the visitor's own. The bridges are the lesson's: the bridge table of konigsberg3d.gd for the axis parity, read from an instance of that script, so the model on the table and the city on the floor are one set. A bridge counts a crossing when a body enters by one end and leaves by the other; crossed once it turns green, twice red. Water holds a body off. Standing on a land's pink plate begins the count again there; the blue plate outside changes the city. When a bridge has been crossed twice, or all once, the lands show the number of bridges at each, red where it is odd. From the way in: 6 of 7 (blocked), 7 of 8 (walk; 8 of 8 from Altstadt), 9 of 9 (circuit), 4 of 4 with Loebenicht never reached (severed).
seven_bridges.qfep_connection: What a structure allows is decided before any route is tried: the body finds out with its feet what the count at each land already says.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: walk and circuit differ by one bridge between the island and the east land: two panels of 2 x 1 m and four traffic pyramids where there was water and a barrier across each mouth, 4 square metres of a city of 168. From the bench's standpoint the city fills about half the frame: 4 / 168 x 0.5 = 1.2 %; a flat rasteriser sees less of the pyramids than the render will, so 0.8 % as the floor. blocked ~ walk differ by the ten-metre footbridge with its rails (12.5 square metres: 3.7 %); severed loses three bridges and leaves a land alone.

way_back.name: A Way Back
way_back.description: Strongly connected groups for a body, with gravity as the arrow: a wedge is walked both ways, a drop of a metre one way. Three places stand in a row, each a metre lower than the last - ONE (2 m up, reached from the hall floor by a ramp of wedges), TWO (1 m up), THREE (a court at floor level) - built from the spatial lab's prefabs through the lab's own adapter: one-metre building cubes, walkable wedges, the blue DO NOT CROSS barrier on every edge that is not a connection, planks where a drop begins. The axis mutuality is the lesson's word: none (drops only: no place has a way back), split (a wedge joins THREE and TWO: two groups and one arrow, the lesson's value on this floor), total (a wedge returns from TWO to ONE: one group). The return is built from inside, by standing still on a plate. Each place lies on a mat in the colour of its group.
way_back.qfep_connection: Being able to get there says nothing about being able to come back: the body learns the difference by dropping a metre.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: split and total differ by one wedge (1 x 1 x 2 m, about 2.2 square metres seen from the side) and by the colour of two mats of 2.6 x 2.6 m, which change from the second group's colour to the first's: 13.5 square metres of flat mat seen at a low angle, perhaps a fifth of that in the picture. The work is 9 x 7 m with its ramp and fills about half the frame: (2.2 + 2.7) / 63 x 0.5 = 3.9 %; a flat rasteriser sees the mats poorly behind the barriers, so 1 % as the floor. none ~ split differ by one wedge and one mat.

plank_price.name: The Price of One More Route
plank_price.description: A minimum spanning tree for a body, with a real price. Seven lands lie in water - the south bank and two rows of three islands - and ten places can take a bridge. A bridge is planks: the channels are one, two or four metres wide, the lengths of the three plank prefabs, so a bridge costs its length. Built from the spatial lab's prefabs through the lab's own adapter: decks of five planks let into the floor, plank rails on the four-metre bridges, the blue DO NOT CROSS barrier on the shores and across the mouth of a place without a bridge, concrete barriers round the edge. Outside the way in lies a map of the city at a fifth of its size: standing still on one of its bridges lays that bridge or takes it away. Each land lies on a mat, green when it can be reached from where the body stands, grey when it is cut off. The cheapest set is six bridges and 12 m with nothing spare; one more bridge costs 4 m and buys the right to lose one; all ten cost 24 m.
plank_price.qfep_connection: The cheapest way to reach everything has nothing to spare: resilience is the price of one more route, paid in planks.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: tree and one_more differ by one four-metre bridge: five planks (4 x 1.25 m, 5 square metres) and two plank rails where there was water and a barrier across each mouth, of a city of 156 square metres. From the bench's standpoint the city fills about half the frame: 5 / 156 x 0.5 = 1.6 %; a flat rasteriser misses the rails, so 1 % as the floor. one_more ~ all differ by three bridges of two metres.

stone_river.name: The Route After a Stone Disappears
stone_river.description: The lesson's river at the size of a body. A river ten cells wide and six deep, a metre a cell, between the hall floor and a fenced north bank that can only be reached over the stones: 34 stones at seed 40, a crossing of seven. A body steps from a stone to a stone that shares an edge; water holds it off. Balls lie on the shortest way from where the body stands to the bank it is making for, found with the tutorial's own breadth-first search (the study's route.gd). The river takes a stone on that way - never the one a body stands on; three can be down at once, the fourth sinking lets the oldest rise. Axis impatience: still (only by a plate), patient (every 20 s), impatient (every 8 s). Built from the tower's prefabs: timber panels, trace balls and concrete barriers through the spatial lab's adapter; the museum tape barrier, the pink triangle sign and tripod work lights from the wider catalogue.
stone_river.qfep_connection: A route is a record of what was available when it was found: the body learns it when the next stone is gone.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The axis is a rate: how often the river takes a stone while a body is on it. On a bench no body stands on the river, so nothing sinks at any value and the three stills are the same picture; the only difference is one line of the board's text. This axis is declared for the map token and is invisible in a still by law - the sweep will say INERT, and that verdict is a fact about the bench, not about the river.

two_travelers.name: Two Travelers
two_travelers.description: One tree, two visiting orders taking turns: the tide lights it level by level (BFS), the diver commits to a branch and backtracks (DFS). Every algorithm is an itinerary. Graph taxonomy rung 9, 2026-08-27.

impatient_river.name: Impatient River
impatient_river.description: A spark commutes across stepping stones on the live AStar3D shortest path; sink a stone and it visibly learns a new river. Shortest is a fact about the whole graph. Graph taxonomy rung 10, 2026-08-27.

the_tree_you_are_in.name: The Tree You Are In
the_tree_you_are_in.description: A pedestal projecting a live miniature of its OWN runtime subtree, rebuilt every second from get_children() - the mirror contains the projection as one honest ellipsis node. You have been standing in a graph all along. Graph taxonomy rung 13, 2026-08-27.

switchboard_constellation.name: Switchboard Constellation
switchboard_constellation.description: The graph SUPER OBJECT: an operator's switchboard grown into a constellation - tree plus refused cycles, a five-cord hub, isles married and divorced on the bridge's own clock, a call on the live AStar3D shortest path, the tide, and a desk engraving with one honest ellipsis. 2026-08-27.
